task: Backend (codemie) support for tool-call confirmation inside sub-assistants: interrupt-capable sub-assistant execution, namespace-aware checkpoint, nested interrupted thoughts and depth-aware Allow/Deny resume, with no silent sub-assistant drop.

key_reasoning.reason: Base XL: LangGraphAgent supervisor build/stream, supervisor coordinator/bootstrap patches, ToolCallConfirmationMixin, ToolCallPendingEvent model, ConversationCheckpointSaver/Service, assistant_factory, assistant_engine_builder, resume handler, and ThreadedGenerator thought tree - several subsystems plus a new abstraction (interrupt-capable sub-assistant execution replacing or augmenting the langgraph_supervisor wrapper). Bumped for touching core shared utilities used by every agent run.

Acceptance criteria are concrete (allow/deny, approve_for_me, customer min policy, reload, top-level unchanged), but key design decisions are open: replace vs augment the supervisor wrapper, how the single-checkpoint saver becomes namespace-aware, and which user-visible error path covers any remaining unsupported case.

No precedent: closest pattern is top-level interrupt_before=[tools] confirmation, which cannot reach sub-graphs inside the opaque langgraph_supervisor 0.0.31 wrapper; checkpoint saver ignores checkpoint_ns; ClassVar pending state is shared across agents; regression risk to handoff/parallel/truncation behaviours. The confirmation is a security gate on write tools (bypass = unconfirmed writes), so the security red flag bumps it from XL to XXL.

About 11-13 backend modules modified (langgraph_agent, mixin, models, checkpoint saver/service, assistant_factory, engine_builder, thread.py, handlers, router, exceptions, supervisor coordinator/bootstrap) plus new sub-assistant execution module and several new test files across agents, service, core and rest_api.

API (resume endpoint/handler), Service/agent runtime, and DB-Persistence (conversation pending_checkpoint/pending_tool_call content changes to carry namespace and depth); no UI in this sub-task. Calibration: the bundled L example (10401) is 22 with similar layer spread; this task sits higher due to novelty and checkpointer redesign, matching the XL example (10303) at 27.

Raw total 26 sits on the 26/27 boundary; Technical Risk at XXL and Component Scope at XXL lean higher per the borderline rule, consistent with the Component Scope red-flag bump that lands the total at 27 (XL).

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from XL to XXL: security-sensitive requirement - tool-call confirmation gates write tools, and the customer min policy / approve_for_me must be enforced for sub-assistants
Component Scope bumped from XL to XXL: touches core shared utilities (ThreadedGenerator thought tree, conversation checkpoint saver) and affects every orchestrator/sub-assistant run

split_recommendation.ordering_note: Ship the foundation (depth-aware thought tree, namespace/depth-aware pending model and checkpoint, no silent drop) first; then build interrupt-capable sub-assistant execution and nested resume on top of it.

slices.title: Nested confirmation foundation and no silent sub-assistant drop
slices.scope: Surface sub-assistant build failures as a clear error naming the sub-assistant and policy instead of silently dropping it; make the thought tree depth-aware (parent lookup and interrupted merge at any depth) and extend the pending-call event and conversation checkpoint to carry namespace/depth.

slices.title: Interrupt-capable sub-assistant execution and nested resume
slices.scope: Run sub-assistants in an interrupt-capable, checkpointed execution in place of or alongside the langgraph_supervisor wrapper so their confirmable tool calls pause the run, emit the interrupted thought nested under the sub-assistant step, and resume (allow/deny, approve_for_me, customer min policy, reload) continues the sub-assistant then the orchestrator, with top-level confirmation unchanged.
slices.depends_on: Nested confirmation foundation and no silent sub-assistant drop
